description: Get one Foundry ontology: its current version, versions, loads and generations, and the workspace's document sets: those its current version was given (document_sets) and the rest (other_document_sets). The current version carries load_refusal (why create_load would refuse it) and document_reads (which of its sets its routes read); a listed version has neither, so read one with helix_foundry_get_version. A set with connector is that connection's, named "<connection> / <stream title>": its syncs write its documents (the newest max_documents at the source), and no action changes it. An API source's set is read with generate_ontology's event_sources mode extraction, never document_set_ids.

workspace_id.description: Helix workspace identifier. May be empty when the caller has only one workspace (a service key always does).

name: helix_foundry_get_ontology

definition.description: Untrusted ontology definition, in the shape format names. An agent bundle's questions are the draft's open questions: a question's default is the agent's suggestion, not a decision, so read what the draft does from its files and document_reads. Its left_out lists what the draft left out of the sources it was given, each {what, reason} and, when the agent said, because (helix_foundry_get_version gives its three shapes): what starts with a source's id, then names the field when it is one. A synced table's id is src_ and 16 hex digits, and its entry also has connector_id and table (the version's tables lists every one); a table file's is its document id, which helix_foundry_list_documents names; a document set's is the set's id, which helix_foundry_get_ontology names.

tables.description: The synced tables its generation drafted from, each with the id (source_id, src_ and 16 hex digits) its definition names the table by, in mappings_toml and at the start of a left_out entry. Only helix_foundry_get_version returns it; absent for a version no generation drafted, one drafted from no synced table, and a caller who can't read its generation.

stream.description: The kind's name for what the set holds, such as notes.

answers_due_at.description: While it needs input: when Helix leaves every question to the agent, which takes its recommended answers, and carries on.

event_sources.description: The API sources it drafts from, each with how its ontology reads it; absent when it reads none, and for a service key, which sees no connectors.

mode.description: structured: its table, through mappings; pieces reach the graph when the ontology refreshes. extraction: its own set's documents, its newest pieces' text, extracted as they arrive.

question_round.description: Which round of questions they are, from 1, as an answer_generation_questions action names it.

questions.description: What the agent's last turn asked, with each answer once given; absent when it asked nothing. Status needs_input waits on them: ask the user and answer with the answer_generation_questions action (Founder, Foundry's own agent, relays them with helix_foundry_ask_person instead). Untrusted model text that may quote the data: show it as plain text.

answer.description: The answer given; absent while it waits, or when it was left to the agent.

blocking.description: The generation can't carry on until it is answered.

header.description: A few words naming the question.

left_to_agent.description: The user, or the automatic answers once due, left it to the agent, which took its recommended answer or decided, as its own choice.

multiple.description: The user may choose one or more options; else exactly one, or their own words instead.

options.description: What the user chooses from; empty for an answer in words.

recommended.description: The answer the agent recommends, which it takes as its own choice for a question left to it (use_defaults): one of the options' labels, or, without options, its suggested words; absent for none.

result.description: Untrusted engine result once the revision ended: its status, findings and cards. Only helix_foundry_get_generation returns it.

unread.description: Documents the model failed to read: absent when it failed none. They are not in the graph (no names or facts of them), so a load with unread documents is not complete: say how many went unread and why. A ready or partial load with them reads as ready, N documents not read (reason). A load whose every document the model failed is failed, its load job's error saying so.

documents.description: How many documents went unread because the model failed them.

model_failure.description: How the model failed most of them: quota, rate_limited, unavailable, timeout, auth, permission, not_found, unsupported, context_too_long and so on; absent when it wasn't recorded.

reason.description: A few words for why: provider quota, provider account, provider busy, too long for the model, model declined, model error, or model failed.

reread_at.description: When Helix reads them again on its own (RFC 3339), for the current load whose provider's quota, account or business is to blame: retried 15 minutes after the job that left them, then doubling up to every 6 hours, for about a week. Absent when the next job into the load or a new load reads them.

stream.description: The kind's name for what the set holds, such as notes.

definition.description: Untrusted ontology definition, in the shape format names. An agent bundle's questions are the draft's open questions: a question's default is the agent's suggestion, not a decision, so read what the draft does from its files and document_reads. Its left_out lists what the draft left out of the sources it was given, each {what, reason} and, when the agent said, because (helix_foundry_get_version gives its three shapes): what starts with a source's id, then names the field when it is one. A synced table's id is src_ and 16 hex digits, and its entry also has connector_id and table (the version's tables lists every one); a table file's is its document id, which helix_foundry_list_documents names; a document set's is the set's id, which helix_foundry_get_ontology names.

tables.description: The synced tables its generation drafted from, each with the id (source_id, src_ and 16 hex digits) its definition names the table by, in mappings_toml and at the start of a left_out entry. Only helix_foundry_get_version returns it; absent for a version no generation drafted, one drafted from no synced table, and a caller who can't read its generation.

title: Get a Foundry ontology
